description:
Run a governed query against the semantic layer: choose an entity, then
    the metrics, dimensions and filters you want. Aliases are resolved to
    physical columns by the registry, so this cannot reach anything the
    semantic model does not expose. The result includes the generated SQL.

    Bounded and self-describing.
    UK only. Costs 50 credits (50p). You are charged if the query reaches the
    warehouse and then times out or errors there; a rejected query is free,
    and so is one that matches no rows. Filter area facts on the
    `analytics_area_id` from area_resolve; they are monthly, so a year
    ("2025") or quarter is widened to its months.

OrderBy.description:
One sort key on a semantic query.

Was `list[list[str]]`, i.e. a list of unnamed pairs. Nothing said whether
an element is ["price", "desc"] or ["desc", "price"], and a positional pair
cannot carry that. Naming the two halves removes the guess.

column.description: Metric, dimension or column ALIAS to sort by. Must be one you also selected.
column.title: Column

SemanticFilter.description:
One filter clause on a semantic query.

Typed rather than a bare dict because the model cannot guess these key
names, and it demonstrably does not: in one session it sent
`{"field": ..., "op": ...}` and then `{"dimension": ..., "operator": ...}`,
and every semantic query in that session failed validation. A
`list[dict[str, Any]]` produces a JSON schema of `additionalProperties:
true`, which tells the caller nothing at all.

Mirrors property_service.api.v1.endpoints.semantic_controller.SemanticFilter.
If that changes, this has to change with it.

column.description: Column or dimension ALIAS on the entity, as returned by the catalog — not a physical column name. e.g. 'uprn'.
column.title: Column

value.description: Scalar for most ops; a list for `in`; a two-element list for `between`.
value.title: Value
